q: Before you start driving, the guide lists five basic habits to do in a set order. Which one comes first?
choices: Fasten your seat belt
Lock your doors
Adjust your mirrors
Adjust your head restraint
hint: The seat belt is the last step, after everything else is set.
explain: The guide's order is: lock your doors, adjust your seat, adjust your head restraint, adjust your mirrors, then fasten your seat belt.
quote: Before driving do the following basic habits in this order: 1 Lock your doors.

q: When you adjust your seat, what is the minimum distance you should be from the steering wheel?
choices: 10 centimetres
50 centimetres
25 centimetres
1 metre
hint: It is more than the ideal gap behind your head, but less than the space you leave beside a car when you start to parallel park.
explain: Sit at least 25 centimetres (10 inches) from the steering wheel, the distance recommended by Transport Canada, while still reaching the pedals and controls.
quote: Adjust your seat and seat back support properly so that you are at least 25 centimetres (10 inches) away from the steering wheel. This is the distance recommended by Transport Canada.
topic: Airbag distance (25 cm) and seat position

q: Where should the centre of an adjustable head restraint be?
choices: Level with the top of your ears
Level with the base of your neck
Level with your shoulders
Level with your chin
hint: It has to sit high enough to support your head, not just your neck, in a collision.
explain: Set the head restraint so its centre is level with the top of your ears. A properly adjusted head restraint protects your head and neck.
quote: If your vehicle has an adjustable head restraint, it should be positioned so that the centre of the head restraint is level with the top of your ears.

q: Your vehicle has air bags. Do you still have to wear a seat belt?
choices: No, air bags replace the seat belt
Only when driving on a highway
Only if you sit in the back seat
Yes, you are still required to wear it
hint: Think about whether air bags and seat belts protect you in the same way.
explain: The law requires you to wear your seat belt, and that does not change in a vehicle with air bags.
quote: You are still required to wear your seat belt when in a vehicle with air bags.

q: You are parked at the right-side curb and want to pull out into traffic. Which signal should you use?
choices: Right turn signal
Left turn signal
Hazard lights
No signal is needed
hint: Think about which way your vehicle moves as it leaves the curb.
explain: Moving away from the right side of the road means moving left into traffic, so use your left turn signal.
quote: If you are moving away from the right side of the road, use your left turn signal to indicate that you are entering traffic.
topic: Signalling: moving away from the curb

q: You are parked on the left side of a one-way road and want to pull out. Which signal should you use?
choices: Left turn signal
Hazard lights
Right turn signal
No signal is needed
hint: Think about which way your vehicle moves to reach the traffic lane.
explain: From the left side of a one-way road you move right to enter traffic, so use your right turn signal. You must always signal when moving away from the curb.
quote: If you are on the left side of a one-way road, use your right turn signal.
topic: Signalling: moving away from the curb

q: You are ready to pull away. You have checked that your path is clear and checked your mirrors. What else must you do to be sure your blind spots are clear?
choices: Sound your horn
Do a shoulder check
Check your inside mirror a second time
Flash your headlights
hint: Mirrors do not show everything beside you.
explain: Before moving, check your path, check your mirrors, and do a shoulder check, because your mirrors cannot show your blind spots.
quote: Check your inside and outside rear view mirrors. Do a shoulder check to be sure your blind spots are clear.

q: In a vehicle with an automatic transmission, in which gear positions will the engine start?
choices: Park or Neutral
Park or Reverse
Drive or Neutral
Reverse or Drive
hint: The engine only starts in positions where no gear is sending power to the wheels.
explain: The engine will start in Park or Neutral. It will not start in Reverse, Drive, Overdrive, or the lower gears.
quote: The vehicle's engine will start when the transmission is in Park. ... The vehicle's engine will start in Neutral.

q: In a vehicle with an automatic transmission, when should you use the lower gears (third, second, or first)?
choices: When you want to save fuel at higher speeds
When you need more power but less speed, such as on hills
When the vehicle is being towed
When you are starting the engine
hint: Think about conditions where you want to stop the transmission from shifting up.
explain: Lower gears give more power but less speed and keep the transmission from shifting to a higher gear. Use them on hills and in slush, gravel, snow, sand, or ice.
quote: To be used when you require more power but less speed and to prevent the transmission from shifting to a higher gear. These gears may be used when going up or down hills
topic: Automatic/manual transmission, low gears on hills

q: Before starting the engine of a vehicle with a manual transmission, how should the gear shift lever and clutch be set?
choices: In first gear, with the clutch pedal released
In neutral, with the clutch pedal released
In reverse, with the clutch pedal pressed halfway
In neutral, with the clutch pedal pressed down completely
hint: You want no connection between the engine and the wheels when the engine starts.
explain: Put the gear shift lever in neutral and press the clutch pedal all the way down before starting a manual transmission vehicle.
quote: When starting the engine of a vehicle equipped with a manual transmission, the gear shift lever should be in the neutral position and the clutch pedal should be pressed down completely.

q: In a manual transmission vehicle, what is the friction point?
choices: The point where pressing the brake pedal harder would lock the wheels
The point where you first feel the engine and transmission connect as you release the clutch
The highest speed you should reach in each gear before shifting up
The point on an icy road where your tires start to lose their grip
hint: It is something you learn to feel when moving off smoothly from a stop.
explain: As you slowly release the clutch pedal, you start to feel the engine and transmission connect before the pedal is fully up. That point is the friction point.
quote: As you begin to release the clutch pedal by slowly lifting your left foot, the connection between the engine and the transmission will begin to be felt before the pedal is fully released. The point where this occurs is called the friction point.

q: For the best vehicle control, where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?
choices: At about 12 o'clock and 6 o'clock
At about 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock
At about 11 o'clock and 1 o'clock
At about 7 o'clock and 5 o'clock
hint: Picture the wheel as a clock face and think about balance and reach.
explain: Place your left hand at about 9 o'clock and your right hand at about 3 o'clock.
quote: To have the best vehicle control, place your left hand at about the 9 o'clock position. Your right hand should be at about the 3 o'clock position.

q: The design of your steering wheel does not allow the usual recommended hand position. Where should you place your hands instead?
choices: At about 10 o'clock and 2 o'clock
Both hands at about 12 o'clock
At about 8 o'clock and 4 o'clock
At about 6 o'clock and 12 o'clock
hint: The backup position still keeps one hand on each side of the wheel.
explain: If 9 and 3 o'clock is not possible because of the wheel design, place your left hand at about 10 o'clock and your right hand at about 2 o'clock.
quote: If this is not possible due to the design of the steering wheel, place your left hand at about the 10 o'clock position and your right hand at about the 2 o'clock position.

q: Which steering method should you use when turning a corner?
choices: One hand at the top of the wheel
Hand-over-hand
One hand at the bottom of the wheel
Both hands together at the top
hint: Think about keeping control of the wheel through a full, sharp turn.
explain: Steer through corners using the hand-over-hand method. To return the wheel, use hand-over-hand or let it slide through your loosened grip.
quote: When turning a corner, steer using the hand-over-hand method.

q: Which of these is a time when you must use your signal light?
choices: Driving straight through an intersection
Following a curve in your lane
Changing lanes
Going up a steep hill
hint: Think about which move takes your vehicle into space another driver may be using.
explain: You must signal when moving away from the curb or parking lane, turning left or right, and changing lanes.
quote: You must use your signal light when you are: moving away from the curb or parking lane turning left or right changing lanes.

q: Which statement about speed matches the guide?
choices: Driving well below the flow of traffic is always the safest choice
Driving too slowly can be a hazard
You may go over the speed limit to keep up with traffic
Quick starts that spin the tires are fine on dry roads
hint: Think about what happens when one vehicle moves much slower than everyone around it.
explain: Driving with the flow of traffic reduces your risk of a collision, and driving too slowly can be a hazard. You must still never exceed the posted speed limit.
quote: Never exceed the posted speed limit. Do not accelerate so quickly that the vehicle's tires spin. Drive with the flow of traffic to reduce the risk of being in a collision. Driving too slowly can be a hazard.
topic: Posted limit = max; driving too slowly

q: Total stopping distance is made up of which three parts?
choices: Reaction distance, braking distance, and skidding distance
Perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance
Perception distance, following distance, and braking distance
Signalling distance, reaction distance, and braking distance
hint: One part happens in your head before your foot even moves.
explain: Total stopping distance = perception distance + reaction distance + braking distance.
quote: Perception distance + Reaction distance + Braking distance = Total stopping distance

q: According to the guide, what is the average reaction time for a driver?
choices: About one-quarter of a second
About three-quarters of a second
About two seconds
About three seconds
hint: It is less than one second.
explain: Reaction time is how long it takes to move your foot from the accelerator to the brake. The average is three-quarters of a second.
quote: Reaction time is how long it takes to respond to a situation by moving your foot from the accelerator pedal to the brake pedal. The average reaction time is three-quarters of a second.

q: What is perception time?
choices: How long it takes to move your foot from the gas pedal to the brake
How long it takes to recognize a situation and understand that you need to stop
How long it takes your vehicle to stop after the brakes are applied
How long you must wait at a stop sign before moving ahead
hint: It all happens in your head, before your foot moves.
explain: Perception time is how long it takes to recognize a situation and understand that you need to stop. It can take about three-quarters of a second, and drivers with less experience often take longer.
quote: Perception time is how long it takes to recognize a situation and understand that you need to stop. This can take about three-quarters of a second. Drivers with less experience often take longer to realize a danger exists.

q: You have to stop quickly. What is threshold braking?
choices: Applying the brakes hard enough to lock the wheels
Applying the brakes without locking the wheels
Shifting into neutral and coasting to a stop
Using only the parking brake to stop
hint: It gives the most braking while you can still steer.
explain: Threshold braking means braking without locking the wheels. Braking efficiency is at its maximum and you can still steer.
quote: If you must stop quickly, use threshold braking. This is applying the brakes without locking the wheels. This is where braking efficiency is at its maximum while still allowing you to steer your vehicle.

q: You are braking hard in a vehicle without anti-lock brakes (ABS) and the wheels lock. What should you do?
choices: Press the brake pedal even harder
Release pressure on the brake pedal slightly
Turn the steering wheel sharply
Press the accelerator
hint: Locked wheels mean you have lost the ability to steer.
explain: If the wheels lock, ease off the brake pedal slightly. Braking hard enough to lock the wheels causes a loss of steering control.
quote: If the wheels lock, release your pressure on the brake pedal slightly. Applying the brakes hard enough to lock the wheels will cause a loss of steering control.

q: Which of these factors that affect your stopping distance is one you can control?
choices: The weather
Your vehicle's speed
How slippery the road is
The speed of the vehicles around you
hint: The guide lists your alertness and the condition of your brakes and tires as factors within your control.
explain: Road and weather conditions affect stopping, but they are not on the guide's list of factors you can control. Your vehicle's speed is on that list.
quote: Many factors affect your stopping time and distance. These include road and weather conditions. Some factors you can control are: ... your vehicle's speed

q: How fast should you go when reversing?
choices: At a crawl or slow walking speed
No faster than 20 km/h
At the speed of nearby traffic
Quickly, to spend less time in reverse
hint: Seeing behind you is hard, so you need lots of time to react.
explain: All reversing must be done at a crawl or slow walking speed.
quote: All reversing must be done at a crawl or slow walking speed.

q: When reversing in a straight line, where should you look?
choices: Only in your inside rear view mirror
Over your left shoulder out the side window
Over your right shoulder through the rear window
Straight ahead through the windshield
hint: Turn your body slightly so you can see directly where the vehicle is going.
explain: Put your left hand at the top of the wheel, shift onto your right hip, and look over your right shoulder through the rear window, glancing to the front now and then.
quote: Look over your right shoulder through the rear window. Reverse slowly while covering the brake pedal.

q: When reversing, which way do you turn the steering wheel?
choices: Opposite to where you want the rear of the vehicle to go
In the direction you want the rear of the vehicle to go
Always to the right first, then straighten
Always to the left first, then straighten
hint: Think about which end of the vehicle you are aiming.
explain: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the rear of the vehicle to go. The front will swing the opposite way.
quote: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the rear of the vehicle to go. Note: The front of the vehicle will move in the opposite direction from the direction the rear of the vehicle is moving.

q: Where is it illegal to move your vehicle in reverse?
choices: Out of a private driveway
Into a parallel parking space
Into an intersection or a crosswalk
Out of an angle parking stall
hint: Think about busy places where other road users cross paths.
explain: It is illegal to reverse into an intersection or a crosswalk. The other choices are normal moves the guide describes, done slowly and carefully.
quote: It is illegal to move your vehicle in reverse into an intersection or a crosswalk.

q: You are reversing out of a driveway onto a street. Where should you stop reversing before you drive forward?
choices: In the nearest traffic lane
In the second traffic lane
Before your vehicle reaches the street
At the far curb of the street
hint: Back out only as far as you need to, then drive forward.
explain: Steer into the nearest traffic lane and then go forward. Do not reverse into a second traffic lane.
quote: When reversing out of a driveway, steer your vehicle into the nearest traffic lane and then go forward. Do not reverse into a second traffic lane.

q: White lights come on at the back of a parked vehicle just ahead of you. What does this tell you?
choices: The driver is about to turn left
The vehicle is in reverse and may move backwards
The vehicle's hazard lights are on
The driver is braking to stay parked
hint: Think about which gear turns on the white or clear lights at the rear.
explain: White reverse lights show that the vehicle is in reverse gear, so be ready for it to move backwards.
quote: If you see white reverse lights on a vehicle, be aware that it may move backwards. These lights show that the vehicle is in reverse gear.

q: When you are parallel parked, what is the farthest your wheels may be from the curb?
choices: 25 centimetres
50 centimetres
1 metre
1.5 metres
hint: It is less than the space you leave beside the other car when you start the parking move.
explain: The law requires the wheels of a parked vehicle to be no more than 50 centimetres from the curb.
quote: The law requires that the wheels of the parked vehicle not be more than 50 centimetres from the curb.
topic: Parked wheels within 50 cm of curb

q: You get out of your vehicle, which is parked at the curb on a two-way street. How should you walk to the curb?
choices: Around the front of the vehicle, with your back to traffic
Around the rear of the vehicle, facing traffic
Along the traffic lane to the nearest corner
Around whichever end of the vehicle is closer
hint: Think about which direction traffic in the nearest lane comes from.
explain: After a shoulder check, open the door only as wide as needed, get out quickly, and walk to the rear of the vehicle facing traffic to reach the curb.
quote: When it is safe, open the door no wider than necessary to get out and leave the vehicle quickly. Walk to the rear of the vehicle facing traffic to get to the curb.

q: When may you enter a perpendicular or angle parking stall that is on your left?
choices: Only when you are in a parking lot
On any one-way street
On any two-way street when traffic is light
On any street that has angle parking
hint: Think about where crossing an oncoming lane to reach a stall is expected.
explain: Only enter a perpendicular or angle parking stall on your left when you are in a parking lot, and check for oncoming traffic before you cross its lane.
quote: Only enter a perpendicular or angle parking stall to your left when you are in a parking lot.

q: You are parking facing uphill on the right side of a street with a curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
choices: To the right, toward the curb
To the left, toward the centre of the road
Straight ahead
It does not matter if the park brake is set
hint: If the vehicle rolls back, you want the back of the front tire to catch against the curb.
explain: Uphill with a curb, turn the wheels left and let the vehicle roll back slowly until the right front tire touches the curb. This helps keep it from rolling into traffic.
quote: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, turn the front wheels to the left (toward the centre of the road). With the wheels turned, allow your vehicle to roll back slowly until the right front tire is touching the curb.

q: You are parking facing uphill on the right side of a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
choices: To the left, toward the centre of the road
Straight ahead
To the right, toward the edge of the road
It does not matter if the park brake is set
hint: With no curb to stop it, you want a rolling vehicle to leave the road, not enter traffic.
explain: Uphill with no curb, turn the wheels right so that if the vehicle starts to move, it goes off the road and not into traffic.
quote: When parking facing uphill on a street without a curb, turn your front wheels to the right (toward the edge of the road). By doing this, if the vehicle starts to move it will go off the road and not into traffic.

q: You are parking facing downhill on the right side of the road. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
choices: To the left, toward the centre of the road
Straight ahead
To the right, toward the curb or road edge
Left if there is a curb, right if there is not
hint: Facing downhill, having a curb or not does not change the answer.
explain: Facing downhill, always turn your front wheels to the right. If the vehicle starts moving, it will go off the road and not into traffic.
quote: When parking facing downhill, always turn your front wheels to the right.

q: To keep a parked vehicle from rolling down a hill, what should you always do?
choices: Set the park brake and use neutral for either transmission
Use park or low gear, but leave the park brake off
Set the park brake and use drive or a high gear
Set the park brake and use park (automatic) or low gear (manual)
hint: Two things work together here: a brake and the right gear.
explain: Always set the park brake, and put an automatic in park or a manual in low gear.
quote: To prevent a parked vehicle from rolling down a hill, always set your park brake and place your transmission in park (for an automatic transmission) or low gear (for a manual transmission).

q: You are parking facing downhill on the left side of a one-way street. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
choices: To the right
To the left
Straight ahead
It does not matter on a one-way street
hint: Think about where the edge of the road is when you are parked on the left side.
explain: Downhill on the right side of the road, you turn the wheels right. On the left side of the road, turn them the opposite way, which is left.
quote: When parking facing downhill, always turn your front wheels to the right. ... When parking on the left side of the road, turn the front wheels in the opposite direction.

q: What is the closest you may park to a fire hydrant?
choices: No closer than 1.5 metres
No closer than 3 metres
No closer than 5 metres
No closer than 10 metres
hint: It is the same distance as the rule for stop signs and marked crosswalks.
explain: Do not park within 5 metres of a fire hydrant. If the hydrant is not at the curb, measure from the point on the curb nearest the hydrant.
quote: within five metres of a fire hydrant. When the hydrant is not located at the curb, do not park within five metres of the point on the curb nearest the hydrant.
topic: No parking within 5 m of a fire hydrant

q: What is the closest you may park to a driveway or the entrance to a garage?
choices: 1.5 metres
50 centimetres
5 metres
10 metres
hint: It is shorter than the distance for fire hydrants.
explain: Do not park within one and a half metres (five feet) of access to a garage, private roadway, or driveway.
quote: within one and a half metres (five feet) of access to a garage, private roadway, or driveway

q: You must not park within how many metres of the nearest side of a marked crosswalk?
choices: 1.5 metres
3 metres
5 metres
10 metres
hint: It matches the rule for stop and yield signs.
explain: Do not park within 5 metres of the nearest side of a marked crosswalk, and never on any part of a crosswalk.
quote: within five metres of the nearest side of a marked crosswalk

q: Which of these is a place where you must not park?
choices: Six metres from a fire hydrant
On the approach to a bridge
Two metres from a driveway
Ten metres back from a stop sign
hint: Compare each distance with the minimums the guide sets.
explain: You must not park on a bridge, an underpass, or the approaches to either. The other places are farther than the minimum distances (5 metres for hydrants and stop signs, 1.5 metres for driveways).
quote: on a bridge or underpass or the approaches to a bridge or underpass

q: If you park on a roadway outside an urban area, how far along the roadway must your vehicle be visible in both directions?
choices: 15 metres
30 metres
60 metres
100 metres
hint: It is far more than the no-parking distances near hydrants and crosswalks.
explain: Outside an urban area, park only where there is a clear passage for other vehicles and your vehicle can be seen for 60 metres (200 feet) in both directions.
quote: unless there is a clear passage for other motor vehicles, and your vehicle can be seen for 60 metres (200 feet) along the roadway in both directions.

q: Outside an urban area, when may you park on the shoulder of a primary highway?
choices: When you want to take photos of the view
When your vehicle cannot move under its own power
When you need to check a map
Whenever traffic is light
hint: The exceptions are about situations you cannot avoid.
explain: Do not park on the roadway, parking lane, or shoulder of a primary highway unless your vehicle cannot move under its own power, an emergency arises, or it is permitted by law.
quote: on the roadway, parking lane, or shoulder of a primary highway except where: your vehicle is incapable of moving under its own power,
